title: Effects of alcohol on sleep/activity rhythms: Focus on Hypocretin/Orexin
text:
This project tests the hypothesis that, in the rat, exposure to alcohol during adolescence induces long-term
changes in sleep and activity rhythms, increases in drinking, that are in part mediated by hypocretin/Orexin
system in key sleep circuits. These studies also test new therapeutics for adolescent alcohol-induced sleep/wake
pathology.

title: AIDS Malignancies Training and Research International Program (AMTRIP)
text: HIV/AIDS is at epidemic proportions in Zambia, where approximately 1.2 million people – representing about 12% of the country's adult population – are infected. Concomitant with this epidemic, the widespread availability of free anti-retroviral treatment in-country has increased the lifespan of HIV-1 infected individuals, resulting in prolonged chronic immunosuppression and increased occurrence of HIV-associated cancers. However, in-country efforts to prevent, diagnose, and manage cancer in Zambia have been hindered by a lack of laboratory facilities, insufficient cancer research infrastructure, and a shortage of trained personnel. Recognizing these critical gaps, the University of Zambia School of Medicine, the University Teaching Hospitals, and the Louisiana State University leveraged the success of a previous Fogarty partnership to establish the AIDS Malignancies Training and Research International Program (AMTRIP) in collaboration with a new lead partner, the Cancer Diseases Hospital (CDH). This unique program aims to enhance Zambia's cancer research infrastructure and capacity by training Zambian biomedical researchers and health care providers in laboratory techniques and research methodology related to basic cancer biology, molecular genomics, and bioinformatics. Now in its fifth year, AMTRIP has made significant strides by providing intensive long-term graduate degree training and short- and medium-term technical training for 25 trainees; hosting workshops for over 300 health care professionals; successfully transitioning trainees into mentorship roles; adapting program activities to meet the needs of trainees and the rapidly changing cancer research landscape; and leveraging partnerships with other D43 programs to expand the program's impact. Building on these accomplishments, this application seeks to further enhance cancer research capacity in Zambia by: 1) continuing to provide long-term academic instruction and research experiences for eight current master's and three current PhD students in Zambia and recruiting four additional master's and two additional PhD students; 2) providing medium-term (six months to one year) technical training for trainees in topics related to molecular pathology, cancer biology, bioinformatics and genomics; and 3) delivering short- term training (less than three months) and technical workshops (3-5 days) designed to enhance basic, clinical, implementation, genomics, bioinformatics, and behavioral cancer research in collaboration with other regional partners and programs. Expected outcomes of this renewal include the graduation of eight current master's and three current PhD candidates; recruitment and training of an additional four master's and two PhD students in relevant cancer research fields; the transition of trainees into mentorship roles; enhanced infrastructure at Zambian institutions, including the completion of a CDH laboratory renovation; and expanded partnerships with other D43 programs. Given current progress and anticipated renewal outcomes, AMTRIP is on track to transition program leadership to the next generation of cancer researchers in a future renewal.

title: Novel tunable metformin-releasing injectable scaffolds to enhance dental pulp stem cell-based craniofacial bone regeneration
text:
Public Health Relevance: The limited intrinsic regenerative potential of large craniofacial bone defects represents a
considerable challenge in oral and maxillofacial surgery. The long-term goal of this proposal is to develop novel tissue
engineering platforms where mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) with functional organic cation transporters belonging to
the solute carrier 22A gene family can be encapsulated within tunable metformin-releasing injectable scaffolds to
potentiate regeneration of vascularized critical-sized bone defects. We anticipate this innovative project will lead to
broader metformin-releasing tissue engineering platforms to benefit many patients in need of oral, craniofacial as well
as orthopedic bone regenerative procedures.

title: Replication study of in vivo postnatal gene editing for metabolic liver disease in the nonhuman primate model
text:
In vivo gene editing via lipid nanoparticle delivery of messenger RNA (mRNA) encoding a gene-editing protein
and a guide RNA (gRNA) offers the potential to treat phenylketonuria (PKU), hereditary tyrosinemia type 1 (HT1)
and other diseases. However, there are currently no clinical-grade LNP formulations available for unrestricted
use by academic investigators. We have developed our own LNP formulation comprising four lipid excipients,
an adenine base editor mRNA, and a gRNA targeting the PCSK9 gene which, when delivered to juvenile
cynomolgus monkeys, resulted in whole liver editing adequate to treat PKU and HT1 and we will now perform
replication studies to validate these findings providing critical information to other academic investigators and for
IND applications for PKU, HT1 and other diseases.

title: Neurodevelopmental defects of the thalamocortical pathway as a convergent feature of psychiatric disorders
text:
We seek to understand the mechanisms underlying human thalamocortical pathway development and to study
how genetic mutations found in patients with neurodevelopmental psychiatric disorders may disrupt the
thalamocortical pathway formation. In order study these processes in human cell-based models, we will take
advantage of human pluripotent stem cell technology which enables scalable in vitro differentiation into tissue
models of the cerebral cortex and the thalamus. Moreover, using cutting-edge single cell sequencing
technologies, we will identify the molecular pathways that may be involved in regulating thalamocortical
pathway development in humans.

title: FastPlex: A Fast Deep Learning Segmentation Method for Accurate Choroid Plexus Morphometry
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because the choroid plexus has been implicated in
neurodevelopment and a range of brain disorders. Evidence demonstrates that the choroid plexus is critical for
brain maturation, immune/inflammatory regulation, and behavioral/cognitive functioning, however current
neuroimaging segmentation tools are poor at accurately and reliably segmenting the choroid plexus. The
proposed studies will utilize large patient cohorts (n=22,000+) from high resolution (Human Connectome Project
and Connectome Related Human Disease) and conventional (inclusive of high risk for psychosis, first episode
and chronic psychosis, bipolar disorder, and Alzheimer's disease) neuroimaging datasets to develop an opensource
deep learning choroid plexus segmentation method that will be used to elucidate changes in the choroid
plexus across the lifespan and within various brain.

title: Molecular mechanisms of mitochondrial complex I rescue by hypoxia and genetic suppressors
text:
Mitochondrial dysfunction is a central driver of age-associated neurodegeneration, including Parkinson’s and
Alzheimer’s disease. Surprisingly, breathing hypoxia rescues mitochondrial mutants in diverse organisms, but
the precise molecular mechanism remains unknown. This proposal combines advanced mitochondrial
genetics with cryoEM microscopy to solve the structures of wild type and mutant electron transport chain
complexes, with the ultimate goal of determining how hypoxia rescues mitochondrial dysfunction.

title: Quantifying Endogenous Transcription and Translation Kinetics in Living Cells
text:
This research will advance our fundamental understanding of how gene expression is regulated in living cells,
revealing dynamic events that are invisible to traditional methods. By developing tools to visualize transcription,
translation, and chromatin modifications at the single-molecule level, we aim to uncover the molecular
principles that govern gene regulation. These discoveries will shed light on core biological processes and lay
the groundwork for future applications in health and disease.

title: AstroTarget™ Astro-Enrichment Kit: A Microfluidic-Free Platform for High-Throughput Rare-Astrocyte Isolation and Multi-Omic Profiling from Frozen Alzheimer’s Brain
text:
Plaque-associated reactive astrocytes, key drivers of Alzheimer’s pathology, make up less than 2% of nuclei in
frozen human brain archives, rendering them prohibitively expensive to isolate and characterize with current
single-nucleus sequencing tools. This project will create the AstroTarget™ Astro-Enrichment Kit-a
microfluidic-free workflow that enriches these scarce nuclei more than 50-fold while capturing both their
transcriptomes and chromatin landscapes, thereby unlocking archived tissue for mechanistic discovery and
therapeutic target identification.

title: Dormancy-dependent determination of hematopoietic stem cell fate from hemogenic endothelium
text:
Transplantation of hematopoietic (blood-forming) stem cells is a life-saving therapy used to cure blood and
immune disorders. However, not all patients in need of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation have suitable
donors of these precious cells. To overcome this obstacle, the research in this proposal seeks to identify the
instructions that guide the initial formation of hematopoietic stem cells during development in order to replicate
their production in the laboratory.

title: Optimizing outcomes for children and young adults with relapse of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia after CD19-targeted chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy
text:
Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy targeting CD19 (CAR19) has revolutionized the treatment landscape
for children and young adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Unfortunately,
however, approximately 50% of children relapse after initial response to CAR19 and their subsequent survival
is dismal. This proposal aims to optimize outcomes after post-CAR19 relapse through two mutually informative
approaches: 1) A phase 1/2 clinical trial testing the delivery of a novel, dual-antigen targeted CAR designed to
overcome the primary mechanisms of CAR19 failure; and 2) An advanced comparative effectiveness study to
determine optimal existing salvage treatment approaches for post-CAR19 relapse.

title: Control of Developmental Timing by NADH Redox Metabolism
text:
The intrinsically slow pace of human development represents a significant limitation for the use of induced
pluripotent stem cells in disease modeling and regenerative therapies. The research proposed in this
application will uncover the role of NADH redox balance in regulating species-specific rates of embryonic
development. This improved understanding of developmental timing will enable us to devise novel strategies to
accelerate human developmental speed, thereby enhancing the therapeutic applications of pluripotent stem
cells.

title: Host and parasite determinants of Leishmania Viannia persistence in naturally infected human populations
text:
The natural history of human dermal leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania Viannia species
provides unequivocal evidence of long-term persistence of parasites in asymptomatically as well as
symptomatically infected individuals. This project aims at studying the role of parasite
subpopulations and characterizing the transcriptomes, metabolomes and immunophenotypes of
host tissues and cells associated with persistent Leishmania infection. It will provide critical
knowledge on the metabolic and immunological microenvironments of human tissues permissive for
Leishmania persistence, define the signatures and biomarkers of persistence, and advance ex vivo
models of persistent Leishmania infection.

title: A multi-scale systems biology framework for understanding and engineering the human gut  microbiome
text:
The human gut microbiome consists of trillions of bacteria that shape our immune system, metabolism and
behavior via a myriad of bioactive microbial metabolites. These metabolites are produced by complex and
dynamic multi-scale interaction networks spanning gene regulatory networks within individual cells to the inter-
species interactions at the community-level. We will revolutionize our ability to decipher these interaction
networks by combining construction of human gut communities from the bottom-up, state-of-the-art techniques
for high-throughput community characterization, advanced computational models of different resolutions, multi-
objective optimization and quantitative measurements of host phenotypes using in vitro and germ-free mouse
models.

title: Understanding How Distinct Heterochromatin States Control Pioneer Factor Binding
text:
Restriction of transcription factor (TF) binding by heterochromatin is essential for spatiotemporal control of gene
expression and proper embryonic development. Despite developmental transitions from gene repression to
activation being often initiated by pioneer factors which overcome the heterochromatin barrier, it remains poorly
understood whether distinct types of heterochromatin differentially regulate DNA accessibility and TF binding.
Here, I will directly compare how G9A/GLP and SETDB1, responsible for histone H3 Lysine 9 di and
trimethylation, respectively, restrict TF and pioneer factor binding to the same gene regulatory sequences.

title: Network medicine-based discovery of therapeutics for knee osteoarthritis
text:
While knee osteoarthritis represents a major public health burden affecting more than 30 million older
individuals in the United States alone, the standard of care is primarily limited to symptom management. This
study will mechanistically interrogate the effects of different exercise protocols, applied in isolation or in
combination with nutritional approaches, on cartilage integrity with aging and according to sex. We anticipate
that the innovative research studies proposed will aid in the development of effective rehabilitation programs
that consider sex-specific variables for the treatment of osteoarthritis.

title: Impact of Aging and Exercise on Glymphatic Function Using Multi-modal MRI
text:
The glymphatic system is brain-wide network supporting the clearance of metabolic waste including amyloid
beta, of which excessive accumulation in the brain can lead to Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, valid
methods for imaging the human glymphatic system are not established. In this project, the research team will
apply a multi-modal MRI approach to comprehensively evaluate the glymphatic system and establish its
effectiveness in capturing glymphatic function changes associated with aging, preclinical AD pathology and
aerobic exercise.

title: Developing and testing a mobile health intervention to promote sun protection behaviors and skin examination among Hispanics
text:
Research on preventing skin cancer among the Hispanic population is needed since melanoma rates are
increasing among Hispanics, and mortality rates are higher than among non-Hispanic whites. The Hispanic
population tends to have misperceptions regarding skin cancer: they are less aware of the symptoms and harms
of skin cancers and are less likely to engage in sun protection behaviors. The proposed project will develop and
pilot test a mobile intervention to increase both sun protection and skin self-examination behaviors among
Hispanic individuals.

title: Project 1: Effects of inflammation on clonal competition and malignant transformation
text:
By unveiling new molecular and pathogenic mechanisms that account for clonal hematopoiesis (CH) and
hematologic malignancies, Project 1 of our Program is tightly aligned with the NCI mission. Our studies will
provide important insights on how the modifiable stressors of infection and high-fat diet-induced obesity exert
selective advantages on hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) with CH-associated mutations and
promote to their malignant transformation. Our discoveries will define the mechanisms by which CH progresses
toward malignancy and provide the groundwork for risk stratification of CH-associated mutations.

title: Regulation of Retinal Ganglion Cell Regeneration
text:
In many diseases of the eye, selective progressive retinal cell loss eventually leads to blindness, necessitating
therapies for replacing the lost cells to restore vision to patients. Intriguingly, the cells responsible for
regenerating retinal cells in fish retain the ability to regenerate retinal cells in mammals, however, fully
awakening this regenerative potential has proven difficult and the results, to date, have been limited. We
propose to use fish models of selective retinal cell regeneration for large-scale genetic screens to define the
genetic programs controlling retinal stem cell regenerative potential and thereby provide insights that will
support the development of regenerative therapeutics for restoring vision to those who have lost it.
